subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The distance-time formula for the motion of a particle along a straight line is S = t³ − 9t² + 24t − 18. Find when and where the velocity is zero.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate and solve v = 0
steps.margin_note: First mark. This is a rectilinear motion question with two asks: when is the time, where is the position. Take the common factor 3 out first — the quadratic then factorises by inspection.
steps.memory_tip: When comes from v = 0 and where comes from S. Two asks, two separate pieces of work.
lines: This is a rectilinear motion question.
the times and also the positions at those times.
(d/dt of t³ is 3t², of 9t² is 18t, of 24t is 24;

lines.text: then take out the common factor 3)

recall.must_convey: That v = 3(t − 2)(t − 4) and that v = 0 at t = 2 and t = 4.
accept: differentiate to get three t squared minus eighteen t plus twenty four
take three common and factorise into t minus two into t minus four
the velocity is zero at two seconds and four seconds
v equals zero pettite t equals two and t equals four vasthundi
there are two times, not one
heard_as: three t squared minus eighteen t

steps.why: The velocity is a quadratic here, so it is zero at two separate instants. Both must be found, because the question then asks where the particle is at each of them.
common_mistakes: Giving only one of the two roots.
Factorising t² − 6t + 8 as (t − 1)(t − 8), which does not multiply back.
Setting the acceleration to zero, which gives the single time t = 3.

steps.label: Find S at each time
steps.margin_note: Second mark: do not answer only 'when'. Put each time back into S. A negative S is a real position — it is 2 units on the negative side of the origin, not a mistake. The particle starts at S(0) = −18 and crosses S = 0 at t = 3 on the way back. The stem prints no units; seconds and metres are the standard reading.
steps.memory_tip: Where means position, and position is given by S. Substitute back into the original formula, never into v.

lines.text: (put 2 in place of t in S)
(put 4 in place of t in S)
(S is in metres and t in seconds)
∴ the velocity is zero at t = 2 sec, where S = 2 m,
and at t = 4 sec, where S = −2 m

recall.must_convey: That substituting the two times back into S gives S = 2 and S = −2.
accept: put the times back into S to find the positions
at two seconds S is two and at four seconds S is minus two
where means the position so substitute into the distance formula
S lo substitute cheste two and minus two vasthundi
the second position is negative, which is allowed

steps.why: 'Where' asks for the position, and the position is given by S, not by v. Substituting the times into v would return 0 both times, which answers nothing.
common_mistakes: Stopping after t = 2 and t = 4 and never finding the positions, which loses half the question.
Substituting the times into v instead of S.
Changing the sign of S = −2 because a negative distance looks wrong.

lines_compact.text: ∴ the velocity is zero at t = 2 sec, where S = 2 m,
and at t = 4 sec, where S = −2 m

insider_note: Two things are wanted: the times AND the positions there. Factor v = 3(t − 2)(t − 4) to get the times, then put each back into S, not into v.
